source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Lower cardiometabolic risk overall because abdominal adiposity is less clinically relevant than total body weight when BMI is normal.","B":"No additional risk information once BMI is known, because waist circumference does not reflect central fat distribution.","C":"Improved insulin sensitivity and lower vascular risk because a larger waist usually reflects greater lean abdominal mass.","D":"Higher cardiometabolic risk because greater waist circumference reflects central adiposity that can add risk information beyond BMI."}}
source_row.rationale: An elevated waist circumference (reflecting central/abdominal adiposity) is associated with increased cardiovascular and metabolic risk (including risk for type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome), since abdominal fat distribution is associated with greater health risk compared to fat distributed in other body areas, making waist circumference a useful adjunct to BMI in cardiovascular risk assessment.
